entries.verseWEB: “The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the broken hearted, to proclaim release to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, to deliver those who are crushed, and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.”
entries.verseKJV: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.
entries.pullShort: preach good news to the poor
entries.pullMedium: preach good news to the poor, heal the broken hearted
entries.pullLong: The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor.
entries.explanation: Jesus reads from Isaiah, announcing his mission. He's addressing those who are often forgotten: the poor, brokenhearted, and oppressed. This isn't abstract; think of someone overlooked in your day-to-day, like the quiet coworker or a neighbor who keeps to themselves. His mission was about real change for real people, offering hope and restoration. It's a reminder that those who seem invisible are seen and valued. You can carry this perspective into your ordinary interactions.
entries.question: Who is overlooked in your daily routine?

entries.verseWEB: Listen, my beloved brothers. Didn’t God choose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom which he promised to those who love him?
entries.verseKJV: Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?
entries.pullMedium: God chose those who are poor in this world
entries.pullLong: God chose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom.
entries.explanation: James speaks to people who may overlook those without wealth. He highlights how richness in faith can reside in those the world sees as poor. Consider a Tuesday where you encounter someone often ignored. Instead of looking past them, recognize the potential richness they hold in aspects that truly matter. It's a reminder that value isn't measured by material wealth but by the depth of one's faith and connection to the promises of the Kingdom.
entries.question: Who might you be overlooking today?

entries.verseWEB: But whoever has the world’s goods and sees his brother in need, then closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him? My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.
entries.verseKJV: But whoso hath this world's good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him? My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.
entries.pullMedium: let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only
entries.pullLong: let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth
entries.explanation: This passage speaks to the practical side of love, especially for those in need. If you have resources and notice someone struggling, the call is to act rather than just express sympathy. It's about moving beyond words to show genuine care through tangible actions. Imagine seeing a colleague who can't afford lunch; offering to buy their meal turns compassion into reality. Real love is displayed through deeds that address immediate needs.
entries.question: How can you turn compassion into action today?

entries.verseWEB: Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, but those who do the truth are his delight.
entries.verseKJV: Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight.
entries.pullMedium: Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD...
entries.pullLong: Lying lips are an abomination to the LORD, but those who do the truth are his delight.
entries.explanation: This proverb highlights the value of honesty in everyday interactions. Imagine a coworker asks about a project status, and it's tempting to embellish your progress. This verse suggests that honesty, even if it reveals less impressive results, is preferable. Being truthful builds trust and integrity. It reminds you that although dishonesty might seem beneficial in the short term, truthfulness has lasting value and is ultimately more satisfying.
entries.question: Where does honesty challenge you today?

entries.verseWEB: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity than he who is perverse in his lips and is a fool.
entries.verseKJV: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, than he that is perverse in his lips, and is a fool.
entries.pullMedium: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity...
entries.pullLong: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity than he who is perverse in his lips and is a fool.
entries.explanation: This proverb contrasts integrity with dishonesty, highlighting that living honestly, even with little, is better than being wealthy but deceitful. Imagine a day at work where someone offers you an easy way to cut corners. Staying true to your values, even when tempted otherwise, keeps your conscience clear and relationships intact. Wealth gained through dishonesty often leads to complications and regrets. Integrity provides peace and respect that outlasts any temporary gain.
entries.question: Where do you find integrity challenging today?

entries.verseWEB: LORD, who shall dwell in your sanctuary? Who shall live on your holy hill? He who walks blamelessly and does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart;
entries.verseKJV: LORD, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill? He that walketh uprightly, and worketh righteousness, and speaketh the truth in his heart.
entries.pullShort: walks blamelessly and does what is right
entries.pullMedium: He who walks blamelessly and does what is right
entries.pullLong: He who walks blamelessly and does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart
entries.explanation: This psalm asks who can be close to God, and answers with honesty and integrity. It's not about perfection, but about living honestly with yourself and others. Imagine a Tuesday where you decide to speak openly about a mistake at work. It might feel risky, but there's a sense of peace in aligning your actions with your values. This passage encourages a heart that values truth, fostering a life that feels right.
entries.question: Where can you practice honesty today?

entries.verseWEB: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
entries.verseKJV: But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
entries.pullMedium: Let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No’
entries.pullLong: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
entries.explanation: In a world full of half-truths and exaggerations, the simple integrity of letting your 'Yes' mean 'Yes' and your 'No' mean 'No' brings clarity and trust. Imagine a Tuesday where you commit to something at work or with a friend. Being straightforward ensures everyone knows where they stand. Overpromising or adding unnecessary explanations can lead to confusion or mistrust. It's about clear, honest communication without embellishments.
entries.question: Where can you simplify your commitments?

entries.verseWEB: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
entries.verseKJV: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
entries.pullMedium: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much.
entries.pullLong: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
entries.explanation: In this passage, Jesus talks about the link between small actions and larger patterns of behavior. Imagine you're at work, tempted to take office supplies home. It might seem insignificant, but this habit can reflect your broader honesty. Small decisions reveal bigger truths about character. Being trustworthy in little things often translates to being reliable when it counts more. You might find that being honest in small stuff makes life simpler and helps you feel more at ease.
entries.question: Where can you practice honesty today?

entries.verseWEB: Therefore, putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbor, for we are members of one another.
entries.verseKJV: Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.
entries.pullShort: speak truth each one with his neighbor
entries.pullMedium: putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbor
entries.pullLong: Therefore, putting away falsehood, speak truth each one with his neighbor, for we are members of one another.
entries.explanation: Paul encourages honesty among people because relationships rely on trust. Imagine at work, where a small lie about meeting a deadline can unravel team trust. Speaking truth strengthens bonds, and everyone knows where they stand. This honesty is not just a moral duty; it’s practical for daily interactions. When you are truthful, you contribute to a community where members can support each other effectively.
entries.question: Where can honesty strengthen your connections today?

entries.verseWEB: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
entries.verseKJV: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.
entries.pullMedium: The life of the body is a heart at peace.
entries.pullLong: The life of the body is a heart at peace, but envy rots the bones.
entries.explanation: This proverb contrasts the effects of peace and envy on well being. It is not a passing feeling but a settled state. Envy can quietly eat at you, like rust working through metal. Maybe a colleague's promotion stings this week. The proverb does not scold the sting. It points at the two directions from here: feeding the comparison, or returning to your own patch of ground. A heart at peace, it says, gives life. Envy only ever takes it.
entries.question: Where do you notice envy affecting your peace?

entries.verseWEB: If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit. Let’s not become conceited, provoking one another, and envying one another.
entries.verseKJV: If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit. Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.
entries.pullMedium: Let’s not become conceited, provoking one another...
entries.pullLong: Let’s not become conceited, provoking one another, and envying one another.
entries.explanation: Paul addresses the community about living in harmony. Envy and conceit can create tension and conflict in relationships. It's easy to feel a twinge of envy when a coworker gets a promotion, but focusing on your own path and growth can bring peace. Living by the Spirit means dropping out of the comparison contest altogether. What is left, once you stop keeping score, is room to actually enjoy the people around you.
entries.question: How does envy affect your relationships?

entries.verseWEB: for you are still fleshly. For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions amongst you, aren’t you fleshly, and don’t you walk in the ways of men?
entries.verseKJV: For ye are yet carnal: for whereas there is among you envying, and strife, and divisions, are ye not carnal, and walk as men?
entries.pullMedium: For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions amongst you
entries.pullLong: For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions amongst you, aren’t you fleshly, and don’t you walk in the ways of men?
entries.explanation: In a community where envy and arguments are common, it's easy to lose sight of what truly matters. You might find yourself comparing your success to others or feeling divided over differing opinions. Imagine being at work on a Tuesday, feeling irritated by a colleague's promotion. This passage reminds you that these feelings are normal, but they can distract you from more meaningful connections and goals.
entries.question: Where do you find envy affecting your relationships?

entries.verseWEB: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, don’t boast and don’t lie against the truth. This wisdom is not that which comes down from above, but is earthly, sensual, and demonic. For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed.
entries.verseKJV: But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth. This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish. For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.
entries.pullMedium: bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart
entries.pullLong: For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed.
entries.explanation: James addresses the destructive power of jealousy and ambition. When these feelings take root, they can lead to chaos and harmful actions. Imagine a Tuesday at work where a colleague's success stirs envy in you. This passage warns that such feelings can disrupt your peace and relationships. Instead of letting jealousy fester, acknowledging it can prevent the turmoil it often brings. Recognizing these emotions helps maintain harmony.
entries.question: Where is envy affecting your peace today?

entries.verseWEB: For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts, covetings, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness. All these evil things come from within and defile the man.”
entries.verseKJV: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man. And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.
entries.pullShort: From within, out of the hearts...
entries.pullMedium: From within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts...
entries.pullLong: For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts, covetings...
entries.explanation: Jesus addresses the source of wrongdoing by pointing to the heart rather than external factors. It's a reminder that the true root of envy and other negative actions comes from within. On a regular day, like a Tuesday at work, you might feel a twinge of envy when a colleague gets recognition. Recognizing that the feeling originates in your own heart can help you address it more honestly. It's about understanding where actions begin.
entries.question: What feelings are brewing inside today?

entries.verseWEB: Let’s walk properly, as in the day; not in revelling and drunkenness, not in sexual promiscuity and lustful acts, and not in strife and jealousy.
entries.verseKJV: Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envying.
entries.pullMedium: not in strife and jealousy.
entries.pullLong: Let’s walk properly, as in the day; not in revelling and drunkenness, not in strife and jealousy.
entries.explanation: Paul addresses behaviors that can disrupt community and personal well-being. He uses the metaphor of daylight, suggesting transparency and honesty in actions. Instead of being consumed by partying, lust, or jealousy, focus on living openly and respectfully. On a regular Tuesday, this might mean choosing to celebrate a colleague's success rather than feeling envious. Such choices foster a peaceful and supportive environment, both for yourself and those around you.
entries.question: Where does envy sneak into your day?

entries.verseWEB: Putting away therefore all wickedness, all deceit, hypocrisies, envies, and all evil speaking,
entries.verseKJV: Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil speakings,
entries.pullMedium: Put away all wickedness, deceit, hypocrisies, envies
entries.pullLong: Putting away therefore all wickedness, all deceit, hypocrisies, envies, and all evil speaking,
entries.explanation: Peter addresses people who were part of communities with challenging social dynamics. Envy can quietly disrupt relationships and personal peace. Imagine scrolling through social media on a Tuesday and feeling a pang of jealousy at someone's success. Peter's advice is simple: let go of that envy. It's not about ignoring others' achievements but finding contentment in your own path. With this mindset, daily interactions become healthier and more genuine.
entries.question: How does envy show up in your life?

entries.verseWEB: The LORD’s law is perfect, restoring the soul. The LORD’s covenant is sure, making wise the simple. The LORD’s precepts are right, rejoicing the heart. The LORD’s commandment is pure, enlightening the eyes. The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring forever. The LORD’s ordinances are true, and righteous altogether.
entries.verseKJV: The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple. The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes. The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the LORD are true and righteous altogether.
entries.pullMedium: The LORD’s law is perfect, restoring the soul...
entries.pullLong: The LORD’s law is perfect, restoring the soul. The LORD’s covenant is sure, making wise the simple.
entries.explanation: The psalmist has spent six verses on the sky, sun and stars preaching without words. Then he turns to the law of the Lord and uses warmer language for it than for the sunrise: perfect, reviving the soul, making wise the simple. For him these are not regulations. They are the same craftsmanship as the heavens, aimed at a human life. Time you spend in them is not homework. It is standing in good light.
entries.question: Where do you go for good light?

entries.verseWEB: How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! Yes, to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.
entries.verseKJV: How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! and to get understanding rather to be chosen than silver!
entries.pullMedium: Better to get wisdom than gold.
entries.pullLong: How much better it is to get wisdom than gold! Yes, to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.
entries.explanation: The verse contrasts wisdom and wealth, urging you to prioritize understanding over material gain. Imagine a Tuesday where you're deciding whether to spend time learning a new skill or chasing extra hours at work for more money. This proverb suggests that investing in wisdom and understanding can offer long-term benefits that money cannot match. It's about valuing knowledge and insight as treasures that can guide you through life's complexities and challenges.
entries.question: What do you value more than wisdom?

entries.verseWEB: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on the rock. The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock. Everyone who hears these words of mine and doesn’t do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand. The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house; and it fell—and its fall was great.”
entries.verseKJV: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock. And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it.
entries.pullShort: built his house on the rock
entries.pullMedium: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew
entries.pullLong: Everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
entries.explanation: In this passage, Jesus contrasts two builders: one wise and one foolish. It's about the stability of your life when challenges hit. On an ordinary day, like when a sudden storm disrupts your commute, having a solid foundation in your values and actions helps you stay steady. Following through on what you know is right provides resilience. Without it, unexpected troubles can feel overwhelming. A stable base makes a real difference.
entries.question: What steadies you when plans collapse?

entries.verseWEB: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words and does them, I will show you who he is like. He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock. But he who hears and doesn’t do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.”
entries.verseKJV: Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock. But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.
entries.pullMedium: He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep.
entries.pullLong: He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep and laid a foundation on the rock.
entries.explanation: Sometimes life feels like navigating a stream that could flood at any moment. Jesus uses this imagery to emphasize the stability that comes from not just hearing his teachings, but truly incorporating them into your actions. It's about the difference between being prepared for challenges and being caught off guard. When the flood eventually comes, and it comes for both builders in the story, the difference is not the weather. It is what the years of quiet obedience already poured underneath.
entries.question: What has your practice been pouring underneath?

entries.verseWEB: The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.
entries.verseKJV: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
entries.pullMedium: I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.
entries.pullLong: The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.
entries.explanation: Jesus speaks of a contrast between destruction and abundance. The idea is simple: some influences take away joy, peace, and purpose, while others enrich life. Imagine scrolling through social media and feeling inadequate. That sense of lack is a thief. In contrast, the life Jesus offers fills you with meaning and purpose. Abundance here isn't about wealth but about fulfillment and peace. It's about living fully in the moment you have.
entries.question: What steals your sense of abundant life?

entries.verseWEB: I know how to be humbled, and I also know how to abound. In any and all circumstances I have learnt the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need. I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
entries.verseKJV: I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
entries.pullMedium: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
entries.pullLong: In any and all circumstances I have learnt the secret both to be filled and to be hungry... I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
entries.explanation: In this passage, Paul talks about learning to find contentment regardless of his circumstances. Whether he's experiencing abundance or need, he's discovered that his strength doesn't come from his situation, but from a deeper source. This isn't about achieving everything you want; it's about finding resilience and peace in any situation. On a regular Tuesday, you might face unexpected challenges, yet this mindset can remind you that external situations don’t define your inner strength.
entries.question: How do you find strength amidst comparison?

entries.verseWEB: For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is able to discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
entries.verseKJV: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
entries.pullMedium: Sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing...
entries.pullLong: The word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
entries.explanation: This passage highlights that the word of God is dynamic and insightful, able to reach the deepest parts of who you are. It’s not just about reading an ancient text, but experiencing something that can reveal your true motivations and intentions. Imagine on a Tuesday, reflecting on a decision you're making. The word helps you see past surface-level reasons and understand your deeper drivers. It’s a tool for honest self-reflection.
entries.question: What intentions are you hiding from yourself?

entries.verseWEB: “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. You shall labor six days, and do all your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any work in it, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates;
entries.verseKJV: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:
entries.pullMedium: “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.”
entries.pullLong: “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. You shall labor six days, and do all your work,”
entries.explanation: In this passage, a rhythm of work and rest is established. Everyone, from family members to animals, takes a break. It's not just about stopping work but recognizing a day set apart for something different. Imagine a Saturday where you put your phone away, and chores can wait, creating space for rest and reflection. The Sabbath isn't about rules; it's about allowing yourself and others the chance to recharge and refresh.
entries.question: How can you create space for rest today?

entries.verseWEB: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.
entries.verseKJV: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
entries.pullMedium: He makes me lie down in green pastures.
entries.pullLong: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.
entries.explanation: This passage describes a shepherd's care, offering both provision and rest. Imagine a quiet park on your day off where you unwind, feeling secure. The shepherd provides what you need, including the space to relax. This isn't just about having enough but about being led to places of peace and rest. On a busy Tuesday, you can find moments of calm and trust in that provision, like a lunch break under a shady tree.
entries.question: Where do you find peace in your week?

entries.verseWEB: He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
entries.verseKJV: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:
entries.pullMedium: “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.”
entries.pullLong: He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.”
entries.explanation: In this passage, Jesus addresses a misunderstanding about the Sabbath. The religious leaders had turned it into a burden, but Jesus reframes it as a gift. Imagine a day when you truly rest, free from your usual tasks. It’s not about following rules but experiencing renewal. Maybe on a busy Tuesday, you pause for ten minutes to breathe and relax. It's a reminder that rest is meant to refresh, not restrict.
entries.question: How can you find rest in your routine?

entries.verseWEB: “If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on my holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of the LORD honourable, and honor it, not doing your own ways, nor finding your own pleasure, nor speaking your own words, then you will delight yourself in the LORD, and I will make you to ride on the high places of the earth, and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father;” for the LORD’s mouth has spoken it.
entries.verseKJV: If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it.
entries.pullMedium: If you call the Sabbath a delight...
entries.pullLong: If you call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of the LORD honourable...
entries.explanation: Isaiah speaks to people who see Sabbath merely as a rule. The challenge is to view it as a delight, a day for honoring what truly matters. It's about setting aside personal agendas, not to follow empty rituals, but to genuinely rest and find joy. Imagine a Sunday where you pause your routine, engage in something meaningful, and let go of the usual rush. That shift might reveal unanticipated joys in simply being present.
entries.question: How can you make rest a delight?

entries.verseWEB: The LORD is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth. He will fulfil the desire of those who fear him. He also will hear their cry, and will save them.
entries.verseKJV: The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth. He will fulfil the desire of them that fear him: he also will hear their cry, and will save them.
entries.pullMedium: The LORD is near to all who call on him in truth.
entries.pullLong: The LORD is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
entries.explanation: This passage speaks to the closeness and attentiveness available to those who genuinely reach out in prayer. It's not about using the right words, but about authenticity and reverence. On an ordinary Tuesday, this might mean pausing amidst your routine to speak honestly about your struggles or hopes. It's comforting to know that this openness is met with understanding and care, offering a sense of peace and support.
entries.question: How can you call out in truth today?

entries.verseWEB: LORD, in the morning you will hear my voice. In the morning I will lay my requests before you, and will watch expectantly.
entries.verseKJV: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.
entries.pullMedium: In the morning I will lay my requests before you...
entries.pullLong: LORD, in the morning you will hear my voice. In the morning I will lay my requests before you, and will watch expectantly.
entries.explanation: This passage describes someone starting their day with prayer. It emphasizes a routine of presenting requests to God and then watching for His response. Picture an ordinary morning where you set aside a few moments before the day’s rush. You might be sipping your coffee, thinking about what lies ahead, and in that quiet moment, you share your concerns or hopes, and then wait, expectantly, to see how the day unfolds.
entries.question: What request will you bring in the morning?

entries.pullLong: Commit your deeds to the LORD, and your plans shall succeed.
entries.explanation: The verse talks about inviting God into your plans and efforts. It's like sharing your to-do list with a trusted mentor who offers guidance, helping you focus on what truly matters. Picture a Tuesday where you feel overwhelmed with tasks. Instead of stressing, you take a moment to reflect and prioritize. By committing your goals in this way, you find clarity and purpose in each step you take.
entries.question: What plans can you share today for guidance?

entries.verseWEB: Also delight yourself in the LORD, and he will give you the desires of your heart.
entries.verseKJV: Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.
entries.pullMedium: delight yourself in the LORD, and he will give
entries.pullLong: delight yourself in the LORD, and he will give you the desires of your heart
entries.explanation: Finding delight in something often means you focus on it with genuine joy and interest. Imagine on a Tuesday, instead of rushing through lunch, you savor each bite, appreciating the flavors. This is like delighting in the Lord—finding joy in your relationship with Him. When your heart aligns with what truly satisfies, your desires naturally follow. It's about finding contentment in the journey, not just the destination.
entries.question: What simple joy can you savor today?

entries.verseWEB: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
entries.verseKJV: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
entries.pullShort: Create in me a clean heart
entries.pullMedium: Create in me a clean heart, O God
entries.pullLong: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
entries.explanation: Starting over can feel overwhelming, especially when past mistakes weigh you down. Psalm 51:10 expresses a desire for a fresh start from the inside out. When you feel stuck on a Tuesday, perhaps after making a decision you regret, consider this: a clean slate begins with a change in your heart. Though challenging, it's a hopeful step forward, allowing you to move beyond yesterday’s choices with renewed purpose.
entries.question: What area of your life needs a fresh start?

entries.verseWEB: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
entries.verseKJV: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
entries.pullShort: Search me, God, and know my heart.
entries.pullMedium: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.
entries.pullLong: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
entries.explanation: This verse is about inviting God to examine your innermost thoughts and intentions, highlighting a desire for honesty and self-awareness. On an ordinary day, you might feel uneasy about a choice or thought pattern. Instead of ignoring it, consider a moment of reflection to understand if it aligns with your values. This openness can guide you toward clearer, more intentional living, offering peace of mind.
entries.question: What part of you needs honest reflection?

entries.verseWEB: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
entries.verseKJV: Heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop: but a good word maketh it glad.
entries.pullShort: A kind word makes it glad.
entries.pullMedium: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
entries.pullLong: Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
entries.explanation: When you're feeling weighed down by anxiety, it can feel like you're carrying a heavy backpack everywhere you go. On a Tuesday, this might mean you're distracted at work or struggling to focus during dinner. A kind word from a friend, family member, or even a stranger can lighten that load and lift your spirits. It's a small reminder that you're not alone, and sometimes, just hearing something positive can make a big difference.
entries.question: Who can you offer a kind word to today?

entries.verseWEB: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
entries.verseKJV: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
entries.pullMedium: teach us to count our days
entries.pullLong: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
entries.explanation: Life can feel like a blur of deadlines and appointments, but this verse invites you to pause and reflect on the passage of time. By recognizing the limited number of your days, you gain perspective, appreciating each moment. It's like realizing that the time spent waiting in line could be used to connect with someone nearby. This awareness brings wisdom, allowing you to focus on what truly matters today.
entries.question: How can you make today meaningful?

entries.verseWEB: Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you. Cause me to know the way in which I should walk, for I lift up my soul to you.
entries.verseKJV: Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; for I lift up my soul unto thee.
entries.pullShort: Cause me to hear your loving kindness
entries.pullMedium: Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you.
entries.pullLong: Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you. Cause me to know the way in which I should walk.
entries.explanation: Starting your day with a focus on kindness and direction can set a positive tone. You may have a busy schedule, but pausing to reflect on what truly matters can help you navigate the day. It’s about seeking guidance before the day begins, like checking a map before a journey. This isn’t about grand gestures but simple awareness, like choosing patience in traffic or gratitude over frustration.
entries.question: When do you pause to seek direction?

entries.verseWEB: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
entries.verseKJV: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
entries.pullShort: Keep your heart with all diligence
entries.pullMedium: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
entries.pullLong: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
entries.explanation: This verse highlights the importance of being mindful of what influences your thoughts and emotions. Just like you might choose healthy food to nourish your body, consider what you allow into your mind. On a Tuesday, this might mean choosing to read a book that uplifts you or avoiding a conversation that drains you. By guarding your heart, you keep the source of your life's direction clear and positive.
entries.question: What influences are you allowing into your heart?

entries.verseWEB: I waited patiently for the LORD. He turned to me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay. He set my feet on a rock, and gave me a firm place to stand.
entries.verseKJV: I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings.
entries.pullShort: He set my feet on a rock...
entries.pullMedium: He brought me up out of a horrible pit...
entries.pullLong: He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet on a rock...
entries.explanation: When you feel trapped in a difficult situation, it can be like being stuck in mud with no firm footing. In those moments, patience can be challenging, especially when you seek relief. The psalmist describes waiting patiently and being heard. Eventually, the feeling of being lifted onto solid ground comes. On an ordinary day, waiting could mean giving yourself time to process emotions before acting. This patience cultivates a sense of stability in uncertain times.
entries.question: Where can patience provide you stability today?

entries.verseWEB: The LORD is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
entries.verseKJV: The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.
entries.pullMedium: The LORD is near to all who call on him
entries.pullLong: The LORD is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
entries.explanation: In moments when you feel alone or overwhelmed, this verse reminds you that genuine prayer is a direct line to comfort. It's not about perfect words or rituals, but truthfulness in your heart. Picture a Tuesday when you're stressed over an endless to-do list. Taking a moment to pause and speak honestly in prayer can bring a sense of peace and connection, knowing you're heard.
entries.question: When have you felt heard in prayer?

entries.verseWEB: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
entries.verseKJV: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
entries.pullMedium: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
entries.pullLong: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
entries.explanation: This proverb is about how friendships can refine and improve you. When you spend time with a friend who challenges your thinking, you both grow. It might be a conversation over coffee where they offer a new perspective on something you’re facing. This is not about criticism, but about mutual encouragement and growth. You leave that interaction feeling sharper and more focused.
entries.question: Who in your life helps you grow?

entries.verseWEB: I have set the LORD always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
entries.verseKJV: I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
entries.pullMedium: Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
entries.pullLong: I have set the LORD always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
entries.explanation: The psalmist talks about a choice to focus on the presence of God in every situation. Imagine heading into a challenging meeting at work or facing a difficult conversation. Remembering you've set God before you can bring a sense of steadiness. You might not feel unshakeable, but this mindset can help you stay grounded, even if everything around seems uncertain.
entries.question: When do you notice your focus shifting?

entries.verseWEB: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.
entries.verseKJV: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
entries.pullShort: slow to anger has great understanding
entries.pullMedium: He who is slow to anger has great understanding
entries.pullLong: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.
entries.explanation: Patience can be a challenge, especially when your coworker forgets a deadline or when traffic is at a crawl. Proverbs suggests that being slow to anger is a sign of wisdom, while a quick temper can lead to poor choices. Next time you're in a frustrating situation, take a deep breath and pause. This pause can help you respond with clarity rather than regret. You can find understanding in patience.
entries.question: When has patience led you to better understanding?

entries.verseWEB: Show me your ways, LORD. Teach me your paths. Guide me in your truth, and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation. I wait for you all day long.
entries.verseKJV: Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths. Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.
entries.pullMedium: Guide me in your truth, and teach me.
entries.pullLong: Show me your ways, LORD. Teach me your paths. Guide me in your truth, and teach me.
entries.explanation: When you're unsure of your next step, this passage reflects a desire for guidance and clarity. Imagine you're facing a decision at work or choosing how to spend your evening. You can pause and seek direction, trusting that clarity can emerge as you focus on what truly matters. This suggests an openness to learning and being led in truth. It’s about being patient and allowing time for understanding to develop.
entries.question: What decision are you seeking clarity on today?

entries.verseWEB: God, you are my God. I will earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.
entries.verseKJV: O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;
entries.pullMedium: My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you.
entries.pullLong: My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.
entries.explanation: In a place where everything feels lacking, you might find yourself yearning for something more than what your day-to-day provides. The psalmist expresses a deep longing for connection with God, comparing it to thirst in a dry land. On a day when you feel empty, like there's no refreshment, think of seeking something deeper. A moment of reflection or quiet can bring the peace you're searching for, even in the busiest of days.
entries.question: Where do you feel a sense of longing?

entries.verseWEB: My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him. He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress. I will never be greatly shaken.
entries.verseKJV: Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation. He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.
entries.pullShort: My soul rests in God alone.
entries.pullMedium: He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress.
entries.pullLong: My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him. He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress.
entries.explanation: In moments when life feels like it's shifting beneath you, finding a place of rest can seem impossible. This psalm reminds you that true rest isn't found in circumstances or things but in a relationship. On a busy Tuesday, when work or family demands weigh heavily, you can find stability and peace by remembering your foundation is not in the chaos but in something unshakeable. It's about trusting that you have a refuge that won't fail.
entries.question: Where do you seek stability when life shifts?

entries.verseWEB: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
entries.verseKJV: Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
entries.pullMedium: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul
entries.pullLong: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
entries.explanation: Imagine a conversation with a friend on a regular Tuesday. The words you choose can genuinely uplift or weigh them down. Proverbs 16:24 reminds you that your words have the power to be as sweet as honey, bringing comfort and strength to those around you. When you notice a friend looking tired or stressed, a kind word or a compliment can be the small gift that brightens their day and eases their burdens.
entries.question: How can your words bring sweetness today?

entries.verseWEB: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the LORD, “He is my refuge and my fortress; my God, in whom I trust.”
entries.verseKJV: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
entries.pullShort: He is my refuge and my fortress
entries.pullMedium: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High
entries.pullLong: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty
entries.explanation: This passage paints a picture of security. When fear tries to take over, it's like a heavy blanket you can't shake off. Imagine a Tuesday morning when everything feels uncertain. You can remind yourself that there is a refuge, a fortress stronger than your fears. It’s about choosing to trust in something bigger, even when life feels overwhelming. It’s a mental shift, not an instant fix, but it changes how you face the day.
entries.question: What fear are you holding onto today?

entries.verseWEB: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the hearts.
entries.verseKJV: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts.
entries.pullMedium: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes
entries.pullLong: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the hearts.
entries.explanation: You might feel sure about your choices, confident that what you're doing is right. But it's easy to overlook your own biases. Honesty involves recognizing that your perspective isn't the only one. Like when you're convinced your idea at work is best, but a coworker points out a flaw you missed. It's not about being wrong; it's about understanding that others can see things you can't. This keeps you open and honest with yourself and others.
entries.question: When have you felt sure, but later realized more was happening?

entries.verseWEB: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
entries.verseKJV: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
entries.pullShort: God is the strength of my heart.
entries.pullMedium: God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
entries.pullLong: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
entries.explanation: Sometimes, you feel utterly drained, both physically and emotionally, like your energy and motivation have vanished. This verse reminds you that even when your own resources are depleted, there is a deeper well to draw from. You can pause and acknowledge that it's okay to feel weak. You don't have to rely solely on your own strength. There's a sustaining presence that offers strength and endurance, even when you can't find it in yourself.
entries.question: Where do you find strength when you feel depleted?

entries.verseWEB: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
entries.verseKJV: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.
entries.pullShort: Hope deferred makes the heart sick
entries.pullMedium: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled
entries.pullLong: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
entries.explanation: This proverb speaks to the frustration you feel when something you've been hoping for seems to never arrive. It’s like waiting for a package that keeps getting delayed. Meanwhile, when your hopes are met, it feels renewing and refreshing, like a tree full of life and growth. On an ordinary Tuesday, consider the small joys and milestones that can sustain your heart as you wait for larger hopes to be realized.
entries.question: What small joys can sustain you today?

entries.verseWEB: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
entries.verseKJV: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.
entries.pullMedium: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs
entries.pullLong: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
entries.explanation: In your daily interactions, misunderstandings can lead to tension. Proverbs 10:12 highlights that while holding onto resentment might seem justified, it often intensifies conflict. Choosing love changes the dynamic. If a colleague forgets to include you on an important email, reacting with understanding instead of frustration can defuse potential conflict. By focusing on a forgiving approach, you create an environment where mistakes are learning moments, not sources of lasting tension.
entries.question: Where can you choose love over conflict?
